findings.evidence: "A promotion copies the image URLs already in the source PR bodies. It does not render or attach again." The Reuse workflow is a two-sentence rule with no steps for fetching the source bodies or assembling the promoted body
findings.fix: Add the sequence: fetch each source PR body (gh pr view <n> --json body), keep every image reference verbatim, apply the one-prefix title rule, then assemble; or route to the title/body assembly sections of references/pr-body.md

findings.evidence: "The `explain-pr-changes` command loads `references/pr-body.md` (none-mode diagram filter and PR body templates) on demand." The only load trigger names another command, so a standalone promotion-body request following SKILL.md never loads the reference
findings.fix: Add a scenario trigger inside the Reuse workflow, e.g. "Read references/pr-body.md when assembling or filtering a promotion PR body outside the explain-pr-changes command; do NOT load it for plain attach or publish runs."

findings.evidence: 21 queries with 12 marked should_trigger true against 9 false, while the pinned guidance is about 20 queries with 8-10 should-trigger and 8-10 should-not-trigger; several positives name the branch or skill literally and so barely test the description
findings.fix: Rebalance to 8-10 positives (drop near-certain positives such as the entry literally running "pr-diagrams related main develop --exclude-pr 40") or add stronger near-miss negatives

findings.evidence: *) die "usage: pr-diagrams.sh repo|related|reviewers|render|capability|publish ..." — usage text appears only on error paths (exit 1 or 2); --help is not a first-class flag and flags, env overrides and exit codes are not documented in one place
findings.fix: Handle --help/-h explicitly: print the six subcommands with their arguments and flags (--exclude-pr, --exclude), the env overrides (PR_DIAGRAMS_MODE, DRAWIO_CONVERTER, PR_DIAGRAMS_PROBE_TIMEOUT) and the exit codes, then exit 0

findings.evidence: gh pr create --repo "$REPO" --base "$BASE" --head "$HEAD" --title "$TITLE" ... — $REPO, $BASE, $HEAD and $TITLE are used in the exact commands but never defined for standalone use; only $AD is glossed as "the caller's scratch directory", which presumes an explain-pr-changes caller exists
findings.fix: Add one sentence before the Attach commands: standalone, $AD is a fresh scratch directory (mktemp -d), $REPO comes from pr-diagrams.sh repo, and $BASE/$HEAD are the target and source branches of the PR being created or edited
